why: The kept slice sl-intent-to-design already serves business intent bi-788 and is not in progress, so it is kept. The shaped slice needs one more feature, fn-898 (the build is given the business intent, never the eval; a check flags each build session that read the evals folder), so it is pulled in as the last feature. No feature is pushed out: fn-795, fn-818 and fn-798 each still serve bi-788. The slice stays testable end to end on its one surface, the Claude Code command line, by its one tester, the product owner, with four features.

decisions.question: Which slice serves this business intent, and does it change?
decisions.answer: The kept slice sl-intent-to-design serves bi-788; it pulls in fn-898 and pushes out nothing.
